added_lines: The National Day for Truth and Reconciliation in Canada is a time to remember the First Nations, Inuit, and Métis children who never returned home from residential schools, and the enduring impacts of this history on survivors, their families, and their communities.
Today, we pause to reflect and honour the resilience and strength of Indigenous Peoples. 💙

As a Canadian company, OpenText is committed to advancing our reconciliation journey through learning, listening, and meaningful conversations. We are honoured to welcome acclaimed Anishinaabe author and advocate
for a conversation on Indigenous history, leadership, and the role of culture in shaping Canada's future.
Throughout the month, colleagues have also had the opportunity to deepen their understanding through community engagement, including volunteering at
’s Eminidowang Kiitigan (Spirit Garden for Everyone) and attending the
Together, these experiences encourage reflection, connection, and learning, helping us build greater awareness and understanding of Indigenous histories, cultures, and perspectives.

As AI agents take on more complex, long-running tasks, the ability to retain context and build on previous interactions becomes increasingly important.
The next frontier of AI isn’t just about agents that can act. It’s about agents that can understand, remember, and operate reliably over time.
